entry:eu-genai-code.note: Final code published 10 Jun 2026; Commission found it adequate 8 Jul, AI Board 9 Jul 2026, covering Art. 50(2), (4), (5). Section 1 examples include Anthropic, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI; Meta absent from the GPAI Code signatories (page updated 7 Oct 2026). Signed metadata, imperceptible watermarks, free detection tools; deployer labelling of deepfakes and public-interest text; drafted by independent experts facilitated by the AI Office; adherence not conclusive; others show adequacy to market-surveillance authorities. Art. 50 applies 2 Aug 2026; Omnibus sets 2 Dec 2026 for systems already on the market.

entry:eu-aia.note: OJ text (headless Chromium): 10^25 FLOP presumption (Art 51(2)); state-of-the-art evaluation incl. adversarial testing (Art 55(1)(a)); cybersecurity for the model and physical infrastructure (Art 55(1)(d)). SB 53 §22757.11(i) and RAISE §1420(9)(a) both use >10^26 operations, so the comparison holds. Link resolves to the OJ text; status 'phasing' fits: the Omnibus (Reg. 2026/1744) staggers high-risk application to 2 Dec 2027 / 2 Aug 2028, while GPAI enforcement started 2 Aug 2026. 'Delegated to the Code of Practice and harmonised standards' (sec) not re-checked beyond Art 55/56.

entry:eu-aia:cov:elicit.note: Art 55(1)(a) requires adversarial testing; the GPAI Code's Appendix 3.2 commits signatories to at least state-of-the-art model elicitation, and Measure 3.2 lists red-teaming among evaluation methods. 'Mandating' describes the Code's commitments for signatories (the Code itself is voluntary).

entry:eu-aia:cov:timing.note: Factual core verified: post-market monitoring is a high-risk provider duty (Art 72(1)); the AI Office supervises GPAI models under Art 88(1); conformity/registration duties are pre-market (Art 49(1)); high-risk Chapter III sections now apply from 2 Dec 2027 / 2 Aug 2028 (Omnibus). The closing claim 'The first regulation to formally split the lifecycle this way' is comparative.

entry:eu-aia:cov:mit.note: Factual core verified: prohibited practices (Art 5(1)); FRIA (Art 27(1)) and registration (Art 49(1)) for high-risk; GPAI copyright policy (Art 53(1)(c)); Art 50(2) machine-readable marking (Omnibus gives pre-Aug-2026 systems until 2 Dec 2026); systemic-risk mitigations (Art 55). 'The most comprehensive deployment-mitigation regime in any binding instrument' is comparative.

edge:eu-aia|eu-aio.note: Art 3(47) defines the AI Office as the Commission's implementation/supervision function; Art 88(1) entrusts Chapter V enforcement to it; the Commission's enforcement page confirms AI Office enforcement from 2 Aug 2026.

gap:elicit.note: Checked: the AI Act addresses elicitation only through adversarial-testing language (Art 55(1)(a)); the non-binding GPAI Code explicitly requires state-of-the-art elicitation (Appendix 3.2). The claims about where elicitation work happens (UK AISI, METR, Apollo, labs) belong to other groups' entries, and 'If those organisations stopped, no binding regulation would compensate' is analytic.

faq:what-does-the-eu-ai-office-do.note: Established by Commission Decision of 24 Jan 2024 within DG CNECT (Art 1); request access/recall (Art 92–93), €15M/3% GPAI fines (Art 101(1)), enforcement from 2 Aug 2026 all verified. 'A centralised role unique within EU regulatory architecture' is contradicted by DSA Art 56(2) (Commission's exclusive powers over VLOP/VLOSE duties).

faq:what-is-the-difference-between-layer.note: Internal: every named example sits in the stated layer in the current map data (eu-aia, cn-genai, kr-ai L2; eu-aio, uk-aisi, caisi 'US CAISI', metr, apollo, averi L4). 'EU AI Office (which enforces the EU AI Act)' is shorthand: exclusive over Chapter V (Art 88(1)), national authorities for most else.

entry:us-eo14179.note: EO 14179 (23 Jan 2025, FR Doc. 2025-02172): §4(a) action plan within 180 days; §5(a) review of EO 14110 actions to suspend, revise or rescind. EO 14148 revoked EO 14110, whose §4.2 required reporting of red-team results for dual-use foundation models (the context's example of measures under review). FR API record shows no revocation (notes cite only EO 14365); EO 14434 renames AI to 'Super Intelligence' for executive-branch usage but does not alter prior Presidential actions (§2(b)). Plan dated July 2025. pow 3/active fit; empty cov set consistent. 'Marks the federal turn…' is framing, carried over.

entry:ca-sb53.note: Chaptered SB 53 (Ch. 138, approved 29 Sep 2025) from the Legislative Counsel bulk archive: TFAIA name; >10^26 operations incl. fine-tuning; $500M revenue for large frontier developers; framework duties incl. thresholds and mitigations (§22757.12(a)); annual review (§22757.12(b)(1)); transparency report before/at deployment (§22757.12(c)); 15-day incident reporting (§22757.13(c)); ≤$1M per violation, AG only (§22757.15); whistleblower protections. EO N-9-26 confirms it took effect in 2026. No 2026 amendment to §§22757.10–16 (LAW_SECTION_TBL). 'First US state law to codify the published-framework norm': SB 53 was signed 29 Sep 2025, RAISE 19 Dec 2025. RAISE Ch. 96 (27 Mar 2026) uses identical 10^26 and $500M definitions. The map link (leginfo) refuses automated clients; its bill_id 202520260SB53 matches the official record.

The map link (leginfo) refuses automated clients; its bill_id 202520260SB53 matches the official record.

entry:ca-sb53:cov:thresh.note: Two tiers verified (§22757.11(i)–(j); transparency report and incident duties on 'frontier developers', framework and civil penalty on 'large frontier developers'). The list of developers the law 'anchors against' (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Meta, xAI) is not in the statute.
entry:ca-sb53:cov:thresh.missing: An official list or filings showing which developers meet both thresholds (Cal OES or AG publish none); Anthropic's own SB 53 framework confirms only Anthropic.

edge:ca-sb53|rsp.note: Anthropic: SB 53 formalises transparency practices responsible labs already voluntarily follow; its RSP has set out its approach since 2023. Consistent with 'codifies the published-framework norm Anthropic exemplified'.

faq:how-is-california-sb-53-different-fr.note: 10^26 and $500M in both; frameworks in both; SB 53 15 days and AG-only penalties; RAISE 72 hours to the DFS office (§1420(16), §1421(3)(a); DIGIT page), AG $1M/$3M (§1427(1)); chapter amendment signed 27 Mar 2026. DIGIT opened the RAISE registration portal on 10 Nov 2026 (no change needed here).

entry:co-aia:cov.note: SB 26-189 Sec. 1 repeals and reenacts Part 17; approved 14 May 2026; takes effect 1 Jan 2027 (Sec. 5(1)); AG enforcement as a deceptive trade practice (acct), disclosure duties (mit), effective date (timing). 'Narrower transparency/consumer-disclosure framework' fair: no algorithmic-discrimination duty remains. AG rulemaking hearing held 26 Oct 2026; rules due before 1 Jan 2027, not yet adopted. The desc's 'was repealed' reads as already in force; the repeal takes effect 1 Jan 2027 (timing nuance raised in pending P-0181).
